blocks.text: Deuteronomy 25 presents legal provisions addressing multiple matters: limits on corporal punishment, treatment of animals, family and land continuity, public shame rituals, and conflict resolution. The chapter's central family provision appears in verses 5-10, establishing a levirate marriage practice requiring a man to marry his deceased brother's widow if the brother left no son, so the first child would perpetuate the dead brother's name. These provisions concern family and land continuity. Related provisions appear in Leviticus 25 and Ruth 4, but must not be treated as descriptions of one identical legal mechanism—each text reflects its own particular context and concerns.
